coding.label: Coding
limitations: This series compares one benchmark only. It is not an overall coding score.
The maximum-effort labels do not define a common compute budget.
Anthropic reports a five-trial average. OpenAI reports results from its research environments or API, which may differ from production.
The sources do not verify that all evaluation harnesses and protocols are equivalent.
The three scores are vendor-reported and are not independently verified.
Numerical ordering is descriptive. Cross-vendor protocol equivalence and statistical significance are not established.
Other publisher results and the AA index remain separate evidence, not extensions of this ranking.
Canonical benchmark results do not establish the performance of an exact provider route or its current Pi effort.
coding.methodology: Compare the reviewed vendor-reported DeepSWE 1.1 score at each model publisher's maximum listed effort. This is a conditional software-engineering benchmark comparison, not overall coding ability.
coding.missingValuePolicy: Null is unavailable, never zero. No substitution from another series, benchmark, effort, or model.
coding.orderingPolicy: Descending supplied score. Equal scores tie; modelKey orders ties for display only. Numerical order does not establish statistical significance.

writing.label: Writing
limitations: AI-judge preference is not human evaluation or objective writing quality.

scale.label: Regularized Bradley-Terry AI-judge score; 50 is an estimated one-in-two chance of beating the average model; not a percentage

selectionPolicy.aggregation: None. Do not combine AI-judge, human, or EQ-Bench scores.
selectionPolicy.effortPolicy: Use the exact source record selected by reviewed identity matching. Preserve its effort and quantization. Do not select maximum score or map to Pi effort.
selectionPolicy.replacementPolicy: Changing the benchmark or selection policy requires an explicit producer methodology review and contract revision.

intelligenceCompatibility.reason: OpenRouter does not expose the index version; numerical agreement does not establish compatibility.

evaluationConditions.attemptPolicy: pass@1 is attempt pass rate over scored rollout attempts. pass@4 is tasks with at least one passing rollout divided by tasks attempted. Context-window failures and agent timeouts are scored failures; provider/verifier/network errors are excluded. Efficiency aggregates are over every scored attempt.
evaluationConditions.selectionPolicy: Highest observed pass@1 among configurations attempting all 113 tasks; retain ties

limitations: Shared-harness methodology is publisher-reported, not independently reproduced.
Reasoning effort and compute differ by model and configuration.
Provider/verifier/network errors are excluded from scored attempt denominators.
Selecting the highest observed configuration introduces selection bias; confidence intervals do not account for that selection.
Run-to-run confidence intervals do not quantify uncertainty over new tasks or real-world workloads.
A configuration that attempted fewer than all 113 tasks is retained as evidence but excluded from the full-task group.

methodology.excerpt: mini-swe-agent is model-agnostic by design: every model gets the same bash tool and the same shared prompt, with no per-vendor editing primitives or model-specific instructions.

excerpts: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1 incorporates 9 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf, FrontierCode 2.0, Terminal-Bench 4.0, AA-Omniscience v1.1, HLE-Diamond, CritPt v2 (Hard Subset), and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1.0.
The Intelligence Index is calculated as a weighted average across four categories: Knowledge Work (25%), Coding (25%), Science (25%), and General (25%).
Incorporated grading robustness improvements from the CritPt authors and regraded all models on CritPt v2
mini-swe-agent is model-agnostic by design: every model gets the same bash tool and the same shared prompt, with no per-vendor editing primitives or model-specific instructions.
`cot` (Chain of Thought): The model processes the problem step-by-step.
`direct`: The model directly provides the answer.
`standard(10 options)`: Uses the standard format of augmented MMMU with ten options.
`standard(4 options)`: Uses the standard format of augmented MMMU with four options.
`vision`: Uses a screenshot or photo form of augmented MMMU.

structuralCompatibility: New sidecar artifact. Does not replace or restructure summary.json.
